name: Fenland

neighbourhoods.name: Wisbech
neighbourhoods.housing: Georgian merchants' houses along the river, Victorian terraces, and post-war estates, with many older houses split into flats or shared homes.

neighbourhoods.name: March
neighbourhoods.housing: Victorian railway-era terraces near the centre with large post-war and newer estates around them.

neighbourhoods.name: Chatteris
neighbourhoods.housing: Brick terraces and semis in the town centre, with newer estates on the edges.

neighbourhoods.name: Whittlesey
neighbourhoods.housing: Older brick houses in the historic centre and suburban estates towards Peterborough.

neighbourhoods.name: Doddington
neighbourhoods.housing: A village of older cottages, bungalows and newer detached houses.

neighbourhoods.name: Leverington
neighbourhoods.housing: A village near Wisbech with cottages, bungalows and detached houses.

neighbourhoods.name: Parson Drove
neighbourhoods.housing: A rural fen village of cottages, bungalows and farm properties.

neighbourhoods.name: Manea
neighbourhoods.housing: A fen village with bungalows and newer estates near its station.

neighbourhoods.name: Coates and Eastrea
neighbourhoods.housing: Linear villages of cottages, bungalows and newer homes east of Whittlesey.

housing: Fenland is a rural district of four market towns, Wisbech, March, Chatteris and Whittlesey, set in flat, low-lying fen farmland. Wisbech has fine Georgian houses but also many older terraces and large houses split into flats and shared homes, often let to agricultural and food-processing workers. Elsewhere bungalows, brick cottages and estates of semis and detached houses are common, and house prices are low for the East of England.
checkinTips: Older terraces and converted houses in Wisbech: check for damp, overcrowding signs and fire safety, and photograph each room's lock and furniture in shared homes.
Homes on peat and clay fen soils: photograph any cracks in walls, sticking doors and uneven floors, which can come from ground movement.
Low-lying homes near rivers and drains: note any signs of past flooding or damp in ground-floor rooms and outbuildings.
Rural cottages and bungalows: record septic tanks or treatment plants, oil tanks and their gauges, and any LPG supply where there is no mains gas.
Georgian and Victorian houses along the Nene in Wisbech: check sash windows, chimney breasts and cellars for damp.
Bungalows with large gardens in fen villages: photograph sheds, fences, hedges and drives so their condition is clear at check-out.
tenantHelp: Tenants with disrepair, damp or safety problems in a private let can contact Fenland District Council's private sector housing team, after first telling their landlord.
